title.narrative: Output 7.5. Increased capacity of Member States to develop fair and effective labour migration frameworks, institutions and services to protect migrant workers

description.narrative: 1. Four Roof Integrated Services Centre of Migrant Resource Centers (LTSA-MRC) in East Lampung, Cirebon, Blitar, and Tulungagung provided MRC services to 1,610 migrant workers (1,399 women). In addition to case management, counseling, information, and outreach, financial literacy training and vocational training are also provided to returnee women migrant workers. The MRC in Tulungagung district received the Indonesian Migrant Worker Award from the Ministry of Manpower for providing the best-integrated services to Indonesian migrant workers. The LTSA-MRC model is a pilot multi-stakeholder partnership between the Indonesian Government, village leaders, frontline service providers, and district-level duty bearers to develop integrated and coordinated gender-responsive services for migrant workers at all stages of their migration journey, under Law No. 18/2017 on the Protection of Indonesian Migrant Workers. The integrated LTSA-MRC model has been recognized by the UN Network on Migration as a good practice in 2022. 2. 13 village regulations were adopted in Tulungagung district and Cirebon districts to improve village-level protection mechanisms, including MRC services, for migrant workers. In Blitar districts, two (2) village decrees were adopted to establish village task forces. 3. Two Joint Commitments (MOUs) on Development in Integrating a Gender-Responsive MRC in Government One-Roof Integrated Services Offices (LTSAs) in Blitar and Tulungagung districts were adopted in 2022 The MOU was officially signed by the Head of Regent (Bupati), the President of the Indonesia Trade Union Confederation for All Workers (KSBSI) and the Secretary-General of the Indonesian Women’s Coalition (KPI), signifying ownership and partnership among diverse stakeholders and the political will to protect the rights of migrant workers. 1. With the support of the European Union, the ILO supported the establishment and operations of the integrated gender-responsive MRCs with the Government One-Roof Integrated Services Centres (LTSAs), and built the capacity of 112 MRC staff to improve their ability to provide gender-sensitive services (including case management and counseling capacity); build their knowledge on complaint mechanisms and referral services for women migrant workers who have experienced violence; support women migrant workers’ organizing; and improve coordination and cross-sectoral collaboration among MRCs, workers’ organizations, duty bearers, and other service providers, including how to strengthen the role of the village authorities in implementing article 42 of Law No. 18/2017. 2. The ILO, with EU support, strengthened the capacity of 438 government officials and service providers at provincial, district, and village levels, through training, and cross-border exchanges, to improve gender-responsive services and information provision to migrant workers, their families, and the larger community, in keeping with Law on the Protection of Migrant Workers (No. 18/2017), and its related guidelines for implementation. 3. The ILO had previously given input to the two draft MoUs on the Development of Integrating a Gender-Responsive MRC in Government One-Roof Integrated Services Offices (LTSAs) in Blitar and Tulungagung districts, and the Gender-Responsive Guidelines on the Provision of Services and Protection of Indonesia Migrant Workers (Implementation of Law 18/17). Following its inputs, it has continued to support their adoption, launch, and implementation (with EU support).

title.narrative: 7.5.2. Number of Member States with new or improved services to protect the labour rights of migrant workers
Output 7.5. Increased capacity of Member States to develop fair and effective labour migration frameworks, institutions and services to protect migrant workers

description.narrative: 1. In 2022, the district government in Cirebon adopted the Joint Commitment (MOU) on the Establishment of Tripartite Plus Forum for Coordination and Social Dialogue on Labour Migration, which will enable migrant workers to join tripartite constituents in village-level policy discussions and dialogues. The Tripartite Plus Forum for Coordination and Social Dialogue on Labour Migration was jointly established with Indonesia’s Migrant Workers Union and Women Crisis Centre of Mawar Balqis. 2. Statistics Indonesia (BPS) adopted guidelines for the government to align the labour migration data of the SDMI with the ILO’s international labour migration statistics (ILMS) database. The guidelines were developed in cooperation with the Ministry of Manpower, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, National Agency for the Protection of Indonesian Migrant Workers and Ministry of Law and Human Rights, and have been used in capacity-building trainings for line ministries. Improved collection, use and sharing of labour migration statistics supports better evidence-based policy-making and service provision for migrant workers. 3. The Ministry of Manpower had drafted a Monitoring Tool for the Implementation of Ministry of Manpower Decree No 294/2020 on the Implementation of Placement in the New Normal Period, in 2022. The Monitoring Tool supports the implementation of the SOPs for private recruitment agencies and private technical and vocational education and training (TVET) institutions for overseas workers. The SOPs themselves require TVETs and placement agencies who are sending Indonesian workers abroad, to adopt occupational safety and health (OSH) principles and follow a survivor-centred approach in their complaint and referral mechanism for cases related to violence, harassment, human and labour rights violations, and COVID-19 infections. In 2023, the Tool will be used in labour inspection as the Labour Inspection Checklist for Placement and Protection of Indonesia Migrant Workers. 1. To ensure that migrant workers, especially women migrant workers, can participate on an equal footing in decision-making processes, ILO, with EU support, and in close cooperation with the Indonesian Government, has initiated village-level Tripartite Plus Forums for Coordination and Social Dialogue on Labour Migration which provide an inclusive platform for migrant workers to voice their demands and aspirations to policymakers and key stakeholders, and to have a say on the effectiveness of government coordination in implementing Law No. 18/2017 and gender-responsive coordinated services for migrant workers. 2. ILO, with the support of the EU, has supported Statistics Indonesia (BPS) to strengthen the One Data Indonesia on International Migration (SDMI) platform initiated by BPS. This support has taken the form of guidelines on aligning the SDMI data collection with the definitions and definitions on International Labour Migration Statistic (ILMS) under the ILO’s central database, ILOSTAT. The guidelines have been adopted and were used to train 30 government officials to build their capacity for ILMS data submission and its alignment with the SDMI. 3. ILO continued to strengthen the implementation of Ministry of Manpower Decree No. 294/2020 on the Implementation of Placement of Indonesian Migrant Workers during the Period of Adaptation to the New Habits, by providing technical inputs (as well as facilitating the inclusion of inputs from other stakeholders) into the drafting process of the Monitoring Tool for the Implementation of Ministry of Manpower Decree No 294/2020 on the Implementation of Placement in the New Normal Period. ILO supported a focus group discussion to test the draft tools with representatives from private recruitment agencies and technical, vocational education and training (TVET) institutions. Recommendations sought to strengthen the means of providing gender-responsive services and to ensure their usage by the Labour Inspectorate.
